title: Where, between 1024 and 4096 bytes, does carved-DEFLATE encoder provenance stop clearing its bar? A third corpus at a 2048-byte carve, disjoint by chunk id from both earlier corpora (a byte-level guarantee for seven of eight content families, not for gutenberg), under the 0007 protocol plus gutenberg-excluded margin clauses in both arms.

scope.one_line: One corpus at a 2048-byte carve, built from 25000 source chunks at index offset 75000 (past corpus A's 0..49999 and corpus B's 50000..74999), one seed, four rungs, measured within-size and with a transfer arm at a matched training rung. It locates, to a factor of two, the window boundary at which the 0007 protocol's bar clears at its 500000-fragment top rung, and does nothing else.
scope.naming_note: The measurement script (tools/pivot/run_carve.py) calls whatever corpus it builds 'corpus B' in its field names - corpus_b_chunk_offset, corpus_b_chunk_id_max - because it was written for 0007. In this preregistration the new corpus is corpus C; the field names are the script's and refer to corpus C throughout.
scope.corpora: Corpus A is the existing 4096-byte corpus, source chunk indices 0..49999. Corpus B is the existing 1024-byte corpus, indices 50000..74999. Corpus C is new: 2048-byte carve, 25000 chunks at index offset 75000, so C shares NO chunk index with A or B. The chunk index IS the generator seed for the seven synthetic content families. For the gutenberg family it is NOT a byte-level guarantee - every gutenberg chunk is a window at a random offset into one shared pool (CORRECTIONS.md 2026-08-31, defect 2) - which is why this preregistration adds a clause on the gutenberg-excluded rows rather than repeating 0007's sentence as if the audit had not happened.
scope.matched_rung: The transfer arm trains on corpus A at exactly 100000 rows (the script banks the count it actually used, and the reader checks it) and is evaluated on corpus C's held-out set. Its margin is scored against corpus C's OWN baselines, which - as in 0007 - are trained on the top rung's 500000 rows, not on 100000: a deliberately harder comparison for transfer, stated here so it is not mistaken for a like-for-like one. The like-for-like size comparison is corpus C's own accuracy at its 100000 rung (banked as within_matched_rung_top1) against corpus A's banked 0.1965 and corpus B's banked 0.1165 at the same rung.
scope.rungs: Four rungs on corpus C: 1000, 10000, 100000, 500000. That is 2.699 decades, as in 0007.
scope.unit: One carved 2048-byte window from the middle of one compressed stream.
scope.model_and_features: The 0003 recipe unchanged: HistGradientBoosting on the 1108-column hand-engineered feature set, explicit validation split, the seven-baseline ladder up to depth-16 trees and logistic regression trained on the same rows as the top rung, null control on shuffled labels. Nothing is tuned for 2048. A recipe change would make this a different question.
scope.why_2048: The record holds two carve sizes and a scope sentence between them: 4096 clears (0003, margins +0.1003 frozen and +0.0583 expanded, at an 800000-fragment top rung), 1024 ties a dumb rule (0007, +0.0099, at a 500000-fragment top rung), and 'valid only at a 4096-byte window' is currently a two-point statement with the boundary unmeasured across a factor of four. 2048 is the geometric midpoint; one run under the 0007 protocol (top rung 500000) bounds, to a factor of two, the size at which that protocol's bar clears. The two protocols' top rungs differ (800000 at 4096, 500000 at 1024 and here), which is why the size comparison this preregistration commits to is at the matched 100000 rung, where all three sizes are measured under the same recipe. The information-side prerequisite is already banked from 512 to 4096 (carve_channel_capacity.json: 20.79 to 20.9125 distinct streams of 26), so a failure here is a modelling result, not an information result, exactly as at 1024.
scope.why_now_despite_the_milestone_sequencing: docs/strategy/MILESTONES.md sequences M3's carve-size arm after M4's buyer evidence, so that sizes are measured because buyers report them. This run deviates from that sequencing, and the deviation is stated as one: no buyer has reported a size, this run does not pretend one has, and M3 proper - the sizes buyers report - still waits for M4. The deviation is accepted because the boundary of the record's own scope statement is a property of the record whatever any buyer says, and because the cost is small. EXTRAPOLATION: on the order of one banked 1024 ladder - 1066.6 build seconds and 11.1-751.5 train seconds per rung on 4 cores, no GPU - basis: same fragment count, same pipeline, carve length between the two banked points; the actual cost will be banked in this run's cost block.
scope.expected_outcome_stated_in_advance: CARVE_FAILS is the expected result. The matched-rung accuracy fell by 0.0800 from 4096 to 1024 and the expanded margin fell from +0.0583 to +0.0099; a margin roughly midway between those two banked values sits below the 0.05 bar. A pass at 2048 would be the surprising outcome, and it is the outcome this preregistration is written so that it cannot be manufactured: the bar is not lowered, the recipe is not tuned, and every added clause can only add a way to fail. The gutenberg-excluded clauses are not expected to be the binding ones - on the 0003 record excluding gutenberg widened the margins, so they are expected to be the slackest of the margin readings - they are there so that a margin carried by leaked rows cannot pass, not because they are expected to bite.
scope.what_this_does_not_cover: Carve sizes other than 2048 (and the banked 1024 and 4096). Encoders absent from the 26-configuration box. Learned representations (0009, 0010). It does not fix the gutenberg pool leak - it bounds it with a clause. It does not establish a buyer, a customer, a user or a partner, and no outcome here could; establishes_a_buyer is emitted False unconditionally.

scope_carve.passes_if: carve_bytes == 2048 and reference_carve_bytes == 4096. The reader is frozen for this size; an artifact at any other size is VOID, not read. carve_bytes is taken from the corpus cache's build metadata (the script refuses a cache built at another carve or offset) and the artifact records its source.

scope_parameters_sealed.passes_if: preregistration == '0011-carve-2048-boundary'; seed == 20260825; chunk_size == 32768 and carve_bytes == 2048, both read back from the corpus cache's build metadata (carve_bytes_source must say so; a legacy cache is VOID); eval_frac == 0.2; the rung ladder is exactly [1000, 10000, 100000, 500000]; n_source_chunks == 25000 (the number of distinct chunk ids in corpus C); within_baselines_trained_on_n == 500000; matched_rung == 100000; transfer_n_train == 100000 (corpus-A rows the transfer model was actually fitted on). Any mismatch is VOID: a run under other parameters is a different preregistration.

within_margin_frozen.passes_if: within_top1 - within_best_trivial_baseline >= 0.05, baselines trained on the same rows as the top rung

within_margin_expanded_gutenberg_exclude.passes_if: within_top1_non_gutenberg - within_best_baseline_expanded_non_gutenberg >= 0.05, both scored on the evaluation rows whose source family is not gutenberg - the rows the chunk-index disjointness guarantee actually covers. New in 0011. A missing field is a failure.

within_slope.passes_if: within_slope_ci95_low > 0, where the interval is the CLUSTER bootstrap over the 5000 held-out source chunks computed by tools/scaling.py fit(groups=eval chunk ids) with 2000 resamples at seed 20260825 - the script banks within_slope_bootstrap_unit == 'cluster', within_slope_n_clusters == 5000 and within_slope_bootstrap_resamples == 2000, and the reader requires all three (a fragment-level interval in that field is VOID). The fitter's cluster branch was added on 2026-09-02, after the 2026-08-31 audit that called for it; the 0006/0007 cluster intervals in audit_rederivations.json were re-derived with 4000 resamples, which that artifact now records.

disjointness.passes_if: n_shared_source_chunks == 0 AND corpora_share_source_chunks is False AND the MEASURED chunk-id range of corpus C is exactly 75000..99999 (corpus_b_chunk_offset == 75000, corpus_b_chunk_id_max == 99999). All are measured by the script from the corpora's chunk-id arrays, not echoed from its command line. Exact, not a lower bound: the sealed corpus is this draw and no other, so it cannot be redrawn at a higher offset and re-read. A validity condition: a corpus that fails it was not the preregistered corpus and the run is VOID. For the gutenberg family this is a chunk-id guarantee only, not a byte-level one, which is what the gutenberg-excluded clauses are for.

transfer_margin.passes_if: transfer_top1 - within_best_trivial_baseline >= 0.05, where transfer_top1 is a model trained on corpus A at 100000 and evaluated on corpus C's held-out set, and the baseline is corpus C's OWN.

transfer_margin_gutenberg_excluded.passes_if: transfer_top1_non_gutenberg - within_best_trivial_baseline_non_gutenberg >= 0.05, both scored on corpus C's evaluation rows whose family is not gutenberg. New in 0011: a 4096-trained model has seen gutenberg-adjacent bytes whatever the chunk ids say, so the transfer reading that the disjointness guarantee actually covers is this one.

validity_first.passes_if: No validity clause fails: scope (carve_bytes == 2048, reference_carve_bytes == 4096, n_rungs >= 4, decades_spanned >= 2.0), within_split_is_grouped_by_source is True, null control within tolerance, and every field the reader needs present and finite (NaN and inf read as absent). A validity failure is VOID - no boundary bracketed, not a negative - so that a broken run can never be spun as a result in either direction.

inputs_tied_to_the_banked_corpora.passes_if: sources_sha256 - the script's own hashes of the ten source files it read - equals the banked sources_sha256 in artifacts/pivot/corpus_manifest.json, and reference_y_sha256 / reference_g_sha256 - the script's hashes of corpus A's label and chunk-id arrays - equal the banked hashes of data/pivot/full_c4096.npz in the same manifest. Otherwise VOID: the corpus was not built from the banked sources, or the transfer model was not trained on the banked corpus A.

transfer_model_reproduces_corpus_A.passes_if: abs(transfer_model_top1_on_reference_eval - reference_matched_rung_top1) <= 0.01, where the first is the transfer model's own accuracy on corpus A's held-out set and the second is corpus A's banked 100000-rung accuracy (0.1965). The recipe and seed are the same, so the model must be the same model to within rounding; if it is not, a transfer failure would be a retraining failure in disguise, and the run is VOID.

margin_arithmetic.passes_if: Every margin clause compares round(a - b, 6) against 0.05 - 1e-9, where a and b are the banked accuracies (rounded to 4 decimals by the script). A margin the artifact prints as 0.0500 therefore passes, and one printed as 0.0499 fails; the binary-float representation of the difference decides nothing.

arms: WITHIN-SIZE at 2048: four rungs, grouped split by source chunk, the seven-baseline ladder trained on the same rows as the top rung, null control on shuffled labels, cluster-bootstrap slope. Unchanged from 0007 except for the carve length.
TRANSFER at a MATCHED rung: corpus A's model at 100000, scored on corpus C's held-out set against corpus C's OWN baselines. A transfer number that beats nothing local is not transfer.

GUTENBERG-EXCLUDED readings of the within-size expanded margin AND of the transfer margin, on the rows the disjointness guarantee actually covers. This is the rival explanation 'the margin is carried by leaked bytes' run as a clause in both arms, not a paragraph.

DISJOINTNESS MEASURED, not echoed: the script counts chunk ids shared between corpus A and corpus C from their g arrays and banks the smallest chunk id present; the reader requires zero shared and a smallest id past both earlier corpora.

VALIDITY FIRST: a run with the wrong scope, a non-grouped split, a leaking null control, or a missing or non-finite field is VOID and brackets nothing. A broken run must not be readable as either a pass or a fail.

PER-FAMILY accuracies at the top rung, for the model and for every baseline, are banked alongside so the decomposition at 2048 can be published the way per_family_curves.json publishes it at 4096. They carry no clause.
stop_rules: Any within-size clause failing is CARVE_FAILS, and the boundary is placed in (2048, 4096]: the task holds at 4096 and at no shorter window this repository has measured. This is the expected outcome and it will be published at the same size as a pass would have been.

Within-size passing while transfer fails is CARVE_SIZE_SPECIFIC, boundary in (1024, 2048], and BOTH halves of its meaning are published: not a failure of the label-factory thesis (one model per carve size costs one compression pass), and a failure of the one-model-reads-a-whole-disk-image story.
Both passing is CARVE_ROBUST, boundary in (1024, 2048]. It does not license quoting the 4096 numbers at 2048; the 2048 numbers are quoted at 2048.
A within-size failure is never softened to CARVE_SIZE_SPECIFIC, whatever the transfer arm says.

A validity failure is VOID: no boundary bracketed, no negative claimed, no positive claimed. VOID is published as VOID, with the failed validity clause named, and is never counted as a CARVE_FAILS or quoted as evidence about the boundary.
A missing or non-finite field reads as VOID. Absence is never a pass and never a fail. In particular a run that did not score the gutenberg-excluded rows is VOID, not a failure of the task.

The within-size slope interval is the cluster-bootstrap interval the script computes over held-out source chunks; the fragment-level interval is banked beside it, labelled superseded, and is never the one the reader gates on.

If the run cannot complete under the container's memory or disk (the 800000 rung of 0003 was capped by a ~13.9 GB ceiling), the result is NOT RUN, filed as such, and nothing in the recipe is changed to make it fit. A smaller top rung is a different preregistration.
This cannot revise 0003, 0006 or 0007. Those verdicts stand whatever this one says, and no outcome here clears G5.

The corpus is one draw: chunk ids 75000..99999 exactly. If the build yields any other range or any other count of distinct chunks, the run is VOID and is NOT re-drawn at another offset under this preregistration; a re-draw is a new preregistration with this one's VOID on the record.

thesis.what_would_make_it_fail_honestly: Not a mechanism - the record has one and it says the failure is NOT localised: artifacts/pivot/feature_ablation.json found every one of six feature subsets degrades from 4096 to 1024 by a ratio between 0.5895 and 0.6275, and the alignment columns in particular carry little (VERDICT.md, 'it is not localised, so it is not cheaply fixable'). The expectation rests on the two banked points alone: the matched-rung accuracy fell by 0.0800 from 4096 to 1024 and the margin fell from +0.0583 to +0.0099, and 2048 sits between them. The boundary is expected to lie above 2048; no claim is made about why.
thesis.what_a_pass_would_mean: That the 0007 collapse is steep and late rather than gradual - the recipe holds at 2048 and loses everything between 2048 and 1024. That would narrow, not remove, the CARVE_FAILS scope, and the transfer arm would then say whether one model or two is needed across the working range.
thesis.what_neither_outcome_means: Neither outcome names a buyer. The milestone map's own kill for the forensic use case - buyers whose carves are predominantly below the working boundary - is a fact about buyers, and this run measures the boundary, not the buyers.

invocation: python3 tools/pivot/run_carve.py --carve 2048 --chunks 25000 --chunk-offset 75000 --cache data/pivot/carve_c2048.npz --out artifacts/pivot/carve_generalisation_2048.json --scores-out artifacts/pivot/carve_rung_scores_2048.json --preregistration 0011-carve-2048-boundary (then python3 tools/readers/carve2048_verdict.py). Every other flag at its default: --rungs 1000 10000 100000 500000, --matched-rung 100000, --seed 20260825, --eval-frac 0.2, --chunk-size 32768, --reference-cache data/pivot/full_c4096.npz. The script's defaults for --out/--scores-out are 0007's banked paths, which is why the paths are spelled out here; the reader rejects an artifact stamped with any other preregistration.
